options: Peter and John
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary
Thomas and Matthew
The Roman guards
questions.explain: Matthew 28:1 states: "Now after the Sabbath, toward the dawn of the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to see the tomb."

questions.q: When the women arrived at the tomb, they found it empty. What message did the angel of the Lord give to them regarding Jesus?
options: "He has been taken by the high priests."
"His disciples have moved Him to Galilee."
"He is not here, for he has risen, as he said."
"You must wait here until He returns."
questions.explain: The angel said to the women, "Do not be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. Come, see the place where he lay." (Matthew 28:5-6)

questions.q: In John 21:1-14, Jesus appeared to His disciples by the Sea of Tiberias (Sea of Galilee). What miraculous event occurred during this appearance?
options: Jesus calmed a massive storm before their eyes.
He helped them catch a huge number of fish after they had caught nothing all night.
He walked on the water towards their boat.
He turned the sea water into fresh drinking water.
questions.explain: Jesus told them to cast the net on the right side of the boat. They caught so many fish (153 large fish) that they were unable to haul the net in, though it was not torn.

questions.q: What is the most critical significance of Jesus Christ's resurrection to Christians today?
options: It proved that Roman methods of execution were ineffective.
It confirms His victory over sin and death, guaranteeing eternal life for believers.
It showed that dead bodies could naturally revive after three days.
It established a new government in Jerusalem.
questions.explain: The resurrection is the cornerstone of Christian faith, signifying that Jesus conquered death and validating His identity as the Son of God. It provides believers with the hope of salvation and eternal life.
